_**User**_

Understabd the requirements for an product.
Build a Support Ticket Management System with the following features:
Create a ticket.
List tickets.
View ticket details.
Update title, description, priority and assignee.
Add comments.
Search tickets by keyword.
Filter tickets by status.
Persist data in a database.
Validate input at the backend.
Display meaningful errors in the UI.
Provide a natural-language question-answering endpoint over ticket history, grounded strictly in real ticket data.
Cite the specific ticket(s) used to produce any assistant answer.
Explicitly indicate when no relevant tickets are found, rather than fabricate an answer.

The following state machine must be enforced by the backend:
OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED

OPEN → CANCELLED
IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED
Invalid transitions must be rejected.
Example:
CLOSED → OPEN       ❌
RESOLVED → OPEN     ❌
CANCELLED → OPEN    ❌

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
This is a large greenfield project.

Requirements are now fully understood. The system needs ticket CRUD, comments, search, filtering, database persistence, backend validation, and a natural-language Q&A endpoint with strict citation rules. A Spring Boot 3 and Java 21 backend will be used.

A React and Vite frontend will be used. The Q&A endpoint will rely on retrieval-based search over ticket history, using an LLM only when relevant tickets are found. If no matches exist, the system will explicitly report that no relevant tickets were found.

No external API keys will be required. The QA endpoint will use deterministic keyword search over tickets and comments, generating answers purely from retrieved data without fabricating responses. A simple BM25-style retrieval approach will power the search.

Spring Boot will be placed at the project root under the `com.company.ticketmanagement` package. The Maven POM will include Spring Web, JPA, validation, PostgreSQL, Flyway, and Testcontainers. Lombok will be avoided in favor of records and explicit constructors. Local development will run PostgreSQL via Docker Compose; H2 is forbidden by testing rules. The next step is designing the JPA entities.

JPA entities are now defined. Tickets hold title, description, status, priority, assignee, and timestamps. Comments link to tickets with body, author, and creation time. Status and priority are enums. The state machine enforces OPEN → IN_PROGRESS or CANCELLED, IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED or CANCELLED, and RESOLVED → CLOSED. API routes are planned for creation, listing with filters, detail view, updates, and status changes.

The comment endpoint will be POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/comments. The QA endpoint will be POST /api/v1/tickets/qa. The React frontend will use Vite and simple CSS with CORS enabled. A state-machine completeness test will be added. The QA service will tokenize questions and search titles, descriptions, and comments for keywords. It will return an explicit no-match message when no relevant tickets exist. Otherwise it will summarize findings deterministically from ticket fields only.

Flyway migrations will be added for database schema evolution. The frontend will have three pages: a searchable ticket list with status filters, a detailed view with comments and an update form, and a QA chat panel. Assignees will be stored as plain strings rather than full user objects. Unit tests will cover the state machine transitions in TicketService. OpenAPI documentation will be skipped unless it proves useful.

The project layout is finalized. Maven will use a standard directory structure with a `frontend/` folder for the React and Vite code. CORS will be configured for localhost:5173. Files will be written in batches.

The TicketStatus enum will enforce the state machine invariant through a `canTransitionTo` method. Each status returns its allowed targets via a switch expression, rejecting invalid transitions such as CLOSED → OPEN.

Validation constraints are now defined. CreateTicketRequest requires title, description, and priority. UpdateTicketRequest accepts optional fields but requires at least one change. TransitionTicketRequest requires a status. AddCommentRequest needs body and author. Search queries will use JPA LIKE on title and description, with optional status filtering. Keyword search will also cover comments. The QA endpoint will be POST /api/v1/qa.

The QA endpoint will return a JSON payload with a `found` flag, the generated answer, and a `citations` array containing matched ticket IDs, titles, and statuses. When no tickets match, it will return an explicit `found: false` message stating that no relevant history was found and that answers cannot be invented. The system will use extractive summarization and simple keyword scoring instead of relying on an LLM that might hallucinate. If a question references a specific ticket ID, the lookup will target that exact record. A README will be included to document how to run the application locally.

I am ready to begin writing files. I will generate the Maven wrapper and POM, add a test profile for Testcontainers, and update the .gitignore. I will also check whether Java is installed before starting the batched file writes.

Spring Boot 3.4.3 will be used with Java 21. Jackson’s JavaTimeModule is auto-configured. Pagination is omitted from the ticket list endpoint. The React frontend will use Vite and TypeScript, calling the API directly and rendering errors from Spring Boot’s ProblemDetail responses.

GlobalExceptionHandler will map MethodArgumentNotValidException to field-level errors. An ErrorCode enum will standardize error codes. Domain exceptions include TicketNotFoundException, TicketStateConflictException, and InvalidTicketUpdateException. Comment and QA controllers will reside in the ticket feature package. TicketMapper will be a Spring component. Frontend CSS will be clean, professional, and accessible.

The frontend will use a distinctive, simple design rather than generic AI styling. Docker Compose will launch PostgreSQL 16 on port 5432. The local application.yml will point to that container. JPA auto-validation will be enabled. A README will be added.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Backend validation will catch ConstraintViolationException for invalid request parameters and HttpMessageNotReadableException for malformed enums.

Jackson invalid enums will return 400 instead of 500. A handler for MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException will catch bad status query parameters. The QA service needs all ticket comments loaded upfront to avoid N+1 lazy loading issues.

A dedicated `findAllWithComments()` query will be added for the QA service to fetch all tickets with their comments in one call. A package-private setter will be added to `Ticket` so unit tests can restore a non-OPEN starting status without reflection.

Tests cannot access package-private setters on the domain entity. Invalid transitions will be tested by walking the valid state machine path to the source status, then attempting the forbidden destination. A helper method will automate this for parameterized tests.

The `bringTo` helper will follow a fixed deterministic path to reach each target status. OPEN is already there. IN_PROGRESS follows OPEN. RESOLVED follows OPEN then IN_PROGRESS. CLOSED follows OPEN then IN_PROGRESS then RESOLVED. CANCELLED is a terminal state reachable from both OPEN and IN_PROGRESS.

The full 5×5 status matrix contains 25 pairs. Five are valid transitions. Twenty are invalid. Same-status moves are also rejected. Parameterized tests will cover every pair to verify the state machine.

Invalid-transition tests will assert that the repository is never saved. The transition method does not explicitly persist the entity; JPA dirty checking handles persistence automatically. The test rule requires verifying no side effects occur when a forbidden status change is rejected.

After a rejected transition, the ticket status will be asserted unchanged. The list search will use a JPQL EXISTS clause on the Comment association. The create flow initializes comments as an empty list. The update path will fetch comments via findByIdWithComments. Jackson’s default FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN setting causes unknown enums to throw HttpMessageNotReadableException, which is currently mapped to 500; a dedicated handler will correct this.

The frontend will be a manual Vite React app with custom package.json, vite.config, and source files. Integration tests will use Spring Boot with a MOCK web environment, MockMvc, and Testcontainers. Planned suites include TicketApiIT, TicketServiceTest, TicketQaServiceTest, and TicketStatusTransitionCompleteness. An empty application-test.yml will be added for service connections. Ticket.java needs its comments collection initialized to satisfy Hibernate.

The QA service will return no match when a question yields no tokens or a ticket ID, preventing searches against empty or stop-word-only queries. Single-word terms like "OPEN" are not treated as stop words, so they will correctly match the OPEN status. Unit tests for the QA service will mock the repository.
</details></think>
